applied.problem: 2.10 V ≈ 90% is one guide's figure (BU-903's table puts 2.10 V at full for 1.265 acid, and 1.225 acid near 2.08 V), so it is untrue of the stationary cell the lesson sets up; '25 °C' is not every maker's reference (one uses 20 °C); top-up water must be distilled.

Topping up with plain water invites tap water, which makers forbid (distilled or demineralised only); and correcting to 25 °C with the 1.67 °C rule is one maker's rule, while others use another reference temperature (one uses 20 °C), so comparing with a maker's mark needs that maker's reference.

The picture pairs a cell full at 1.225 with a voltmeter reaching 2.12 V, though rested voltage follows acid strength and 1.225 acid rests lower; and it does not say a hydrometer only works on cells you can open, so sealed cells have one gauge, not two.
